about: Built-in workflow templates (07/10/2026). Sources and reasoning: HPS-Audit-2026-09-24/WORKFLOW-TEMPLATES-RESEARCH.md. Steps name no bot: on use, Dockyard asks who does the work (the other steps) and who checks it (check_steps). Every save runs the engine's validator; tests/test_builtin_workflow_templates.py holds these to it.

templates.name: reach-a-goal
templates.title: Reach a goal
templates.summary: Works towards a goal one thing per round until your 'done when' test holds.
templates.based_on: GitHub Next Goal; the Ralph loop

nodes.title: Write the goal and when it's done
nodes.body: Write the goal in one or two sentences and a 'done when' test anyone can check: a command, a list or a number. Note what is out of bounds.

nodes.title: Your sign-off on the goal
nodes.body: Check the goal and its 'done when' test before any work starts.

nodes.title: Do the next most important thing
nodes.body: Do one thing that moves the goal forward, check it, and note what changed and what to do next. Finish the round as done when the 'done when' test holds; otherwise finish it as stuck with a note on what to do next, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Summarise what changed
nodes.body: List what changed, with the evidence that the 'done when' test holds.

nodes.title: Check the result against the goal
nodes.body: Run the 'done when' test yourself, without relying on the worker's notes, and list anything that isn't met.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: improve-a-number
templates.title: Improve a number
templates.summary: Tries one change per round and keeps it only if the number gets better.
templates.based_on: GitHub Next Autoloop and Daily Perf Improver; karpathy/autoresearch

nodes.title: Set the number and the target
nodes.body: Write the command that measures the number (speed, bundle size, test time, warnings), run it three times for a steady baseline, and set the target. List the files that may change.

nodes.title: Your sign-off on the measure
nodes.body: Check the measurement is fair and the target is worth it.

nodes.title: Try one change and measure it
nodes.body: Make one change, measure it the same way, and keep it only if the number improves; otherwise undo it and log what was tried. Finish the round as done when the target is reached; otherwise finish it as stuck with the log of what was tried, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Check the gain
nodes.body: Measure again from a clean checkout. Confirm the gain, and that nothing else got worse.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: migrate-step-by-step
templates.title: Migrate step by step
templates.summary: Moves a framework, library or language over one slice at a time, with no regressions.
templates.based_on: GitHub Next Crane; Airbnb's and Google's LLM migrations

nodes.title: Inventory and plan the slices
nodes.body: List everything that has to move and split it into slices small enough to finish in one round, each with a check that it still works.

nodes.title: Your sign-off on the plan
nodes.body: Check the slices and their order. More than 10 slices needs a second run.

nodes.title: Migrate the next slice
nodes.body: Migrate the next slice on the list and run the full test suite. Never leave a slice half done. Finish the round as done when every slice has moved; otherwise finish it as stuck with a note of the next slice, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Final full check
nodes.body: Run every test and check on the migrated code and compare its behaviour with before. List any regressions.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: work-through-a-checklist
templates.title: Work through a checklist
templates.summary: Turns a brief into small checked items and does one per round until all are ticked.
templates.based_on: the Ralph loop; Superpowers; the feature-list-as-contract pattern

nodes.title: Turn the brief into a checklist
nodes.body: Break the work into small items, each finished in one round and each with a check that shows it is done. Keep the checklist where every round can read it, and don't change it once agreed.

nodes.title: Your sign-off on the checklist
nodes.body: Check every item is small and has a check.

nodes.title: Do the next unticked item
nodes.body: Pick the most important unticked item, do only that item, run its check, tick it, and note anything the next round should know. Finish the round as done when every item is ticked; otherwise finish it as stuck with the next item named, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Review against the checklist
nodes.body: Run every item's check yourself and list anything that isn't really done.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: try-several-keep-the-best
templates.title: Try several, keep the best
templates.summary: Three independent attempts, picked by a check you can run, then the winner is polished.
templates.based_on: Agentless; AIDE; best-of-N sampling

nodes.title: Set the task and the check
nodes.body: Write the task and the check that will pick the winner: tests, a benchmark or a rule you can measure. The attempts must not see each other.

nodes.title: Attempt A
nodes.body: Solve the task your own way, without looking at the other attempts. Run the check and record the result.

nodes.title: Attempt B
nodes.body: Solve the task without looking at the other attempts, taking a different approach from the most obvious one. Run the check and record the result.

nodes.title: Attempt C
nodes.body: Solve the task without looking at the other attempts, with the simplest approach that could work. Run the check and record the result.

nodes.title: Compare and pick the best
nodes.body: Run the check on all three attempts and pick the best by its result, not by how it reads. Say why, and what the others did better.

nodes.title: Polish the winner
nodes.body: Improve the winning attempt with what the others did better. Finish the round as done when the check passes; otherwise finish it as stuck with what is left, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: find-the-breaking-change
templates.title: Find the change that broke it
templates.summary: Halves the range of changes each round until one is left, then fixes or reverts it.
templates.based_on: git bisect; research on LLM-assisted bisecting

nodes.title: Write a check that shows the problem
nodes.body: Write a command or test that fails on the bad version and passes on a known good one. Run it three times on each, so it gives the same answer every time.

nodes.title: Test the change halfway between
nodes.body: Test the change halfway between the last good and the first bad version, mark it good or bad, and halve the range (git bisect does this). Ten rounds narrow about a thousand changes to one. Finish the round as done when one change is left; otherwise finish it as stuck with the new range, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Explain the culprit
nodes.body: Read the change that broke it and explain in plain words what went wrong.

nodes.title: Fix or revert
nodes.body: Fix the problem, or revert the change if a fix is risky, and show that the check now passes.

nodes.title: Review the fix
nodes.body: Check the fix is right and that the check and the other tests pass.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: run-experiments
templates.title: Run experiments
templates.summary: Runs one experiment per round, keeps what helps, and writes up what worked and what didn't.
templates.based_on: karpathy/autoresearch; Agent Laboratory; The AI Scientist

nodes.title: Plan the experiments
nodes.body: Write the question, the measure, the time or budget per experiment, and a short list of experiments to try, cheapest first.

nodes.title: Your sign-off on the plan
nodes.body: Check the measure is fair and the budget is acceptable.

nodes.title: Run the next experiment
nodes.body: Run one experiment from the list, record the result in the log, and keep the change only if the measure improves. Finish the round as done when the list is finished or the target is met; otherwise finish it as stuck with the result logged, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Write up the results
nodes.body: Summarise every experiment from the log with its numbers, including the ones that failed, and what to try next.

nodes.title: Check the write-up against the log
nodes.body: Check every number and claim in the write-up against the log, and list anything that doesn't match.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: plan-then-build
templates.title: Plan, then build
templates.summary: Explores and plans first, then builds with tests after your sign-off.
templates.based_on: Claude Code's explore, plan, code; GitHub Spec Kit

nodes.title: Explore the code
nodes.body: Read the code involved and list what the change touches. Change nothing yet.

nodes.title: Write the plan
nodes.body: Write the plan: what changes, in which files, how it will be tested, and what is out of scope.

nodes.title: Your sign-off on the plan
nodes.body: Check the plan before any code is written.

nodes.title: Build it with tests
nodes.body: Build the plan with tests, running the whole test suite each round. Finish the round as done when every test passes; otherwise finish it as stuck with what is failing, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Review the change
nodes.body: Review the change against the plan: correctness, tests and anything risky. List what must change.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

nodes.title: Merge
nodes.body: Merge the change once it is signed off.

templates.name: test-first-change
templates.title: Test-first change
templates.summary: You sign off the failing tests first; then the smallest change makes them pass.
templates.based_on: Superpowers' test-driven development; TDFlow; AgentCoder

nodes.title: Write the failing tests
nodes.body: Write tests that describe the new behaviour. Run them and make sure they fail for the right reason. Change no other code.

nodes.title: Your sign-off on the tests
nodes.body: Check the tests describe what you want; the build is held to them.

nodes.title: Make the tests pass
nodes.body: Write the smallest change that makes the tests pass, without editing the tests. Run the whole suite each round. Finish the round as done when every test passes; otherwise finish it as stuck with what is failing, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Tidy up, tests stay green
nodes.body: Clean up the new code without changing what it does, running the tests after each step.

nodes.title: Review the change
nodes.body: Review the change and check the tests were not edited to pass.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: fix-a-reported-bug
templates.title: Fix a reported bug
templates.summary: Reproduces the bug with a failing test, then fixes it without touching that test.
templates.based_on: Agentless; SWE-agent; TDFlow

nodes.title: Reproduce it with a failing test
nodes.body: Write a test that fails because of the reported bug. Change no other code yet.

nodes.title: Find where it goes wrong
nodes.body: Narrow the cause down to the files and functions involved, and say why they are wrong.

nodes.title: Fix it
nodes.body: Change the code until the new test passes and every other test still passes. Never edit the new test to make it pass. Finish the round as done when every test passes; otherwise finish it as stuck with what is failing, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Tell me what was tried
nodes.body: Say what was tried, what failed and where it stopped.

nodes.title: Review the fix
nodes.body: Check the new test really shows the bug and the fix is right.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: fix-failing-ci
templates.title: Fix failing CI
templates.summary: Finds the cause of a red build and fixes it until CI is green; tells you if it gets stuck.
templates.based_on: GitHub Next CI Doctor and PR Fix

nodes.title: Find the cause
nodes.body: Read the failing CI run and find the root cause, with the log lines that show it.

nodes.title: Fix it
nodes.body: Fix the cause, not the symptom, and run CI again. Finish the round as done when CI is green; otherwise finish it as stuck with the new failure, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Tell me what was tried
nodes.body: Say what was tried, what is still failing and why.

nodes.title: Review the fix
nodes.body: Check the fix deals with the root cause and doesn't just silence the failure: no skipped or deleted tests.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

nodes.title: Merge
nodes.body: Merge the fix once it is signed off.

templates.name: upgrade-a-dependency
templates.title: Upgrade a dependency
templates.summary: Reads what changed, bumps the version, then fixes one breakage per round.
templates.based_on: wshobson's deps-upgrade; Byam; BUMP

nodes.title: Read what changed
nodes.body: Read the release notes between the old and new versions and list the breaking changes that touch this project.

nodes.title: Change the version
nodes.body: Update the version and the lock file. Nothing else.

nodes.title: Fix what broke
nodes.body: Fix one breakage per round using the build output and the release notes, then build and test again. Finish the round as done when the build and the tests pass; otherwise finish it as stuck with what is still broken, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Tell me what's left
nodes.body: List what still breaks, what was tried, and whether rolling back is safer.

nodes.title: Review the changes
nodes.body: Check each change against the release notes and look for behaviour that changed without breaking the build.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: check-a-ui-change
templates.title: Check a UI change on screen
templates.summary: Makes the change, then checks and fixes it on screen until nothing is off.
templates.based_on: the rendered UI finish gate pattern; Claude Code best practices

nodes.title: Make the change
nodes.body: Make the UI change and note which screens and states it affects.

nodes.title: Check it on screen and fix
nodes.body: Open the screens at phone and desktop sizes, take screenshots, and try the empty, loading and error states and the keyboard. Compare with the design, list the differences and fix them. Finish the round as done when nothing is off; otherwise finish it as stuck with what is left, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Second look at the screenshots
nodes.body: Look at the final screenshots yourself against the design, in light and dark themes, and list anything off.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: review-with-three-reviewers
templates.title: Review a change with three reviewers
templates.summary: Correctness, security and conventions reviews side by side, then fixes until the checks pass.
templates.based_on: Zeroshot; GitHub Next's reviewers; Claude Code writer/reviewer

nodes.title: Describe the change
nodes.body: Summarise the change under review: what it does, which files, and how it was tested.

nodes.title: Review for correctness
nodes.body: Review the change for bugs, missed cases and missing tests. List findings with file and line, most serious first.

nodes.title: Review for security
nodes.body: Review the change for security problems: inputs, secrets, permissions and dependencies. List findings with file and line.

nodes.title: Review against conventions
nodes.body: Review the change against the project's conventions and readability. List findings with file and line.

nodes.title: Combine the findings
nodes.body: Merge the three reviews, drop duplicates, and order the findings by how serious they are.

nodes.title: Fix the findings
nodes.body: Fix the findings, most serious first, and run the checks. Finish the round as done when every serious finding is fixed and the checks pass; otherwise finish it as stuck with what is left, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: raise-test-coverage
templates.title: Raise test coverage
templates.summary: Adds tests for untested code that matters, keeping only tests that pass reliably and add coverage.
templates.based_on: Meta's TestGen-LLM; GitHub Next Daily Test Improver

nodes.title: Find valuable untested code
nodes.body: Measure coverage and list the untested code that matters most: risky, often changed or often broken.

nodes.title: Write tests
nodes.body: Write tests for the next item on the list. Keep a test only if it builds, passes three runs in a row and raises coverage. Finish the round as done when the list is covered; otherwise finish it as stuck with the next item named, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Review the new tests
nodes.body: Check each new test asserts real behaviour, not just that code runs, and would fail if the code broke.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: security-sweep
templates.title: Security sweep
templates.summary: Scans read-only, ranks the findings, then fixes the urgent ones until a rescan is clean.
templates.based_on: Looper's security-scan; GitHub Next Daily Malicious Code Scan

nodes.title: Scan for problems
nodes.body: Scan the project read-only for exposed secrets, personal data and known vulnerabilities. Change nothing.

nodes.title: Rank the findings
nodes.body: Rank the findings by how serious and how likely they are, and mark which are urgent.

nodes.title: Fix the urgent ones
nodes.body: Fix the urgent findings, then scan again. Finish the round as done when the rescan finds nothing urgent; otherwise finish it as stuck with what is left, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Check the fixes
nodes.body: Scan again yourself and check each fix really closes its finding.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: explore-the-app
templates.title: Explore the app like a tester
templates.summary: Three user journeys tried side by side; findings are reproduced, ranked and filed.
templates.based_on: GitHub Next Daily Adhoc QA; GPTDroid

nodes.title: List the main journeys
nodes.body: List the three most important things a user does in the app, and where each starts.

nodes.title: Try journey 1
nodes.body: Use the app as a new user would for the first journey. Try odd inputs, going back and slow connections. Note anything broken, confusing or slow, with the steps to reproduce it.

nodes.title: Try journey 2
nodes.body: Use the app as a new user would for the second journey. Try odd inputs, going back and slow connections. Note anything broken, confusing or slow, with the steps to reproduce it.

nodes.title: Try journey 3
nodes.body: Use the app as a new user would for the third journey. Try odd inputs, going back and slow connections. Note anything broken, confusing or slow, with the steps to reproduce it.

nodes.title: Reproduce and rank the findings
nodes.body: Reproduce each finding. Drop the ones that don't reproduce, merge duplicates, and rank the rest by how much they hurt users.

nodes.title: Your sign-off on the list
nodes.body: Check the ranked list before anything is filed.

nodes.title: File them as tasks
nodes.body: File each finding as a task with the steps to reproduce it, what was expected and what happened.

templates.name: red-team-an-ai-feature
templates.title: Red-team an AI feature
templates.summary: Attacks an AI feature three ways side by side, then fixes its guards until the attacks fail.
templates.based_on: garak; Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models

nodes.title: List what could go wrong
nodes.body: List how this AI feature could be misused or fail: prompt injection, leaking private data, harmful or made-up answers, misuse of its tools.

nodes.title: Attack: injection and misuse
nodes.body: Try to make the feature ignore its instructions or misuse its tools. Record every attempt and whether it got through.

nodes.title: Attack: data leaks
nodes.body: Try to make the feature reveal private data, secrets or its hidden instructions. Record every attempt and the result.

nodes.title: Attack: harmful or made-up answers
nodes.body: Try to get harmful, biased or made-up answers. Record every attempt and the result.

nodes.title: Rank the failures
nodes.body: List the attacks that got through, most serious first, and keep them all as a test set.

nodes.title: Fix the guards
nodes.body: Fix the most serious failure, then rerun every attack in the test set. Finish the round as done when none get through; otherwise finish it as stuck with what still gets through, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: tune-a-prompt
templates.title: Tune a prompt against test cases
templates.summary: Changes a prompt one edit per round, keeping an edit only if the score on agreed cases goes up.
templates.based_on: DSPy; ERGO; evaluation-driven prompt workflows

nodes.title: Collect the test cases
nodes.body: Gather 20 or more real examples, including ones it gets wrong today, and write what a good answer must do for each. Set a few aside as unseen examples.

nodes.title: Your sign-off on the test cases
nodes.body: Check the cases and what counts as a pass.

nodes.title: Change the prompt, one edit per round
nodes.body: Make one change to the prompt, score it on the test cases, and keep it only if the score goes up. Count passes rather than asking an AI to judge. Finish the round as done when it reaches the target; otherwise finish it as stuck with the score log, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Check on unseen examples
nodes.body: Score the final prompt on the examples set aside, and compare it with the original prompt.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: docs-follow-code
templates.title: Docs follow code
templates.summary: Fixes the docs, never the code, until the link check and the docs build pass.
templates.based_on: GitHub Next Daily Documentation Updater and Link Checker; Looper's docs-sync

nodes.title: Find where docs and code disagree
nodes.body: Compare the docs with the code and recent changes, and list every place they disagree.

nodes.title: Fix the docs
nodes.body: Fix the docs to match the code; never change the code. Run the link check and the docs build. Finish the round as done when both pass and the list is done; otherwise finish it as stuck with what is left, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Check the docs against the code
nodes.body: Spot-check the changed pages against the code and confirm no code changed.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: write-an-onboarding-guide
templates.title: Write an onboarding guide
templates.summary: Writes a getting-started guide, then follows it from scratch until a fresh setup works.
templates.based_on: RepoAgent; the codebase Q&A and onboarding pattern

nodes.title: Map the project
nodes.body: List the main parts of the project, how they connect, and how to install, run and test it.

nodes.title: Write the getting-started guide
nodes.body: Write a guide that takes a newcomer from nothing to a working setup and a first small change.

nodes.title: Follow the guide from scratch
nodes.body: In a clean environment, follow the guide word for word and fix every step that fails or is unclear. Finish the round as done when a fresh setup works from the guide alone; otherwise finish it as stuck with the step that failed, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: triage-the-backlog
templates.title: Triage the issue backlog
templates.summary: Labels, links duplicates and asks for missing details in batches of 20, then hands you the decisions.
templates.based_on: GitHub Next Issue Triage; the classify-then-act pattern

nodes.title: Write the triage rules
nodes.body: Write the labels, what counts as a duplicate, what a good report needs, and what always needs a person.

nodes.title: Your sign-off on the rules
nodes.body: Check the rules before any issue is touched.

nodes.title: Triage the next 20 issues
nodes.body: Take the next 20 untriaged issues: label them, link duplicates, ask for missing details, and flag anything that needs a person's decision. Close or change nothing else. Finish the round as done when none are left; otherwise finish it as stuck with how many remain, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Summarise for me
nodes.body: Summarise what came in, what looks urgent, and which issues need your decision.

nodes.title: Your decisions
nodes.body: Decide the flagged issues.

templates.name: investigate-an-incident
templates.title: Investigate an incident
templates.summary: Tests one likely cause per round until one is confirmed; you sign off the fix.
templates.based_on: wshobson's incident-response; FixItFlow; the incident-to-eval pattern

nodes.title: Gather what happened
nodes.body: Collect the alerts, logs, recent changes and what users saw, with times.

nodes.title: List likely causes
nodes.body: List the likely causes, most likely first, each with the evidence for and against it.

nodes.title: Test the next cause
nodes.body: Check one cause against the evidence. Finish the round as done when a cause is confirmed with evidence; otherwise finish it as stuck with what ruled it out, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Tell me it's unresolved
nodes.body: Say which causes were ruled out, what is still unknown, and what would help.

nodes.title: Your sign-off on the fix
nodes.body: Check the cause and the proposed fix before anything changes.

nodes.title: Apply the fix
nodes.body: Apply the agreed fix and confirm the problem has stopped.

nodes.title: Write the incident review
nodes.body: Write what happened, why, what fixed it and what stops it happening again, and add a check or test that would have caught it.

templates.name: prepare-a-release
templates.title: Prepare a release
templates.summary: Runs every check, writes release notes for people, and publishes after your sign-off.
templates.based_on: Keep a Changelog; semantic-release

nodes.title: Run every check
nodes.body: Run the full test suite, the build and any release checks. Stop if anything fails.

nodes.title: Write the release notes
nodes.body: Group the changes since the last release as Added, Changed, Fixed and Removed, written for the people who use the project. Call out anything that breaks or needs action.

nodes.title: Check the notes against the changes
nodes.body: Check every merged change is in the notes and every note matches a change.

nodes.title: Your sign-off on the release
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

nodes.title: Tag and publish
nodes.body: Tag the version and publish the release with its notes.

templates.name: research-report
templates.title: Research report
templates.summary: You agree the outline; three sections are researched side by side; then a draft is revised.
templates.based_on: GPT Researcher; Looper's research-synthesis; STORM

nodes.title: Plan the outline
nodes.body: Write the question, who the report is for, and an outline of three sections.

nodes.title: Your sign-off on the outline
nodes.body: Check the question and the three sections.

nodes.title: Research section 1
nodes.body: Research the first section of the outline from first-hand sources. Note where every claim comes from.

nodes.title: Research section 2
nodes.body: Research the second section of the outline from first-hand sources. Note where every claim comes from.

nodes.title: Research section 3
nodes.body: Research the third section of the outline from first-hand sources. Note where every claim comes from.

nodes.title: Write and revise the report
nodes.body: Write the report from the three sections, review it against the question and the outline, and revise it. Finish the round as done when every claim has a source and the question is answered; otherwise finish it as stuck with what is missing, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Check the claims against their sources
nodes.body: Check every claim against its source and list any that the source doesn't support.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: draft-critique-refine
templates.title: Draft, critique, refine
templates.summary: A first draft, then critique-and-refine rounds until it meets the brief: posts, docs, emails.
templates.based_on: Self-Refine; Anthropic's evaluator-optimizer

nodes.title: Write the first draft
nodes.body: Write a first draft from the brief: who it is for, what it must do, and how long it should be.

nodes.title: Critique and refine
nodes.body: Critique the draft against the brief (clarity, accuracy, length, tone), then rewrite it. Finish the round as done when it meets the brief; otherwise finish it as stuck with what is still weak, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Read it fresh
nodes.body: Read the latest draft against the brief without the earlier versions, and list anything that still falls short.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: challenge-a-plan
templates.title: Challenge a plan
templates.summary: Two critics side by side, what could fail and what it costs, then the plan is revised.
templates.based_on: GitHub Next Adversarial PM; pre-mortems; Anthropic's voting

nodes.title: Write up the plan
nodes.body: Write the plan on one page: the goal, the steps, the cost and the timeline.

nodes.title: What could fail
nodes.body: Imagine the plan failed a year from now. List the most likely reasons, most likely first.

nodes.title: Cost and reversibility
nodes.body: List what the plan costs in money, time and attention, and how hard each part would be to undo.

nodes.title: Revise the plan
nodes.body: Revise the plan to deal with the most serious risks and costs, and say what changed and what was accepted. Finish the round as done when every serious point is dealt with; otherwise finish it as stuck with what is open, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: fact-check-a-draft
templates.title: Fact-check a draft
templates.summary: Lists every claim, checks each against sources without the draft's wording, then corrects it.
templates.based_on: Chain-of-Verification; Loki

nodes.title: List the claims to check
nodes.body: List every factual claim in the draft: names, numbers, dates and quotes.

nodes.title: Check each claim
nodes.body: Check each claim on its own against original sources, without reading the draft's wording, and note its source or that it failed.

nodes.title: Correct the draft
nodes.body: Fix or cut every claim that failed, add the sources, and recheck the changed lines. Finish the round as done when every claim checks out; otherwise finish it as stuck with the claims still open, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.

templates.name: make-a-decision
templates.title: Make a decision
templates.summary: Makes the case for each option side by side, compares them against what matters, then you decide.
templates.based_on: MADR decision records; L-MAD; the opponent-processor pattern

nodes.title: Frame the decision
nodes.body: Write the question, the options and what matters most: cost, risk, time and how easy it is to undo.

nodes.title: Make the case for option A
nodes.body: Make the strongest honest case for option A, with evidence, and name its biggest weakness.

nodes.title: Make the case for option B
nodes.body: Make the strongest honest case for option B, with evidence, and name its biggest weakness.

nodes.title: Make the case for option C
nodes.body: Make the strongest honest case for option C, with evidence, and name its biggest weakness.

nodes.title: Compare the options
nodes.body: Score each option against what matters and give the strongest argument against the leading one. Don't judge by how well a case is written.

nodes.title: Your decision
nodes.body: Choose an option, or send it back with a question.

nodes.title: Write the decision record
nodes.body: Record the decision, the options considered, why, and the consequences, in the project's decision log.

templates.name: feedback-to-themes
templates.title: Turn feedback into themes
templates.summary: Groups feedback into named themes, checks them on a sample, and turns the top ones into tasks.
templates.based_on: TopicGPT; GitHub Next Discussion Task Miner

nodes.title: Gather the feedback
nodes.body: Collect the feedback (issues, reviews, support messages, survey answers) and note where each piece came from.

nodes.title: Group it into themes
nodes.body: Name each theme in plain words with a short description and two example quotes. Merge themes that overlap.

nodes.title: Check the themes on a sample
nodes.body: Take 20 pieces of feedback at random and check each fits a theme; fix the themes where they don't. Finish the round as done when they all fit; otherwise finish it as stuck with the ones that don't, and the next round carries on from there.

nodes.title: Turn the top themes into tasks
nodes.body: Turn the three biggest themes into tasks, each with the evidence behind it.

nodes.title: Your sign-off
nodes.body: Read what was done and the evidence before saying yes.
